## Passages
RESULT [webresearch]: Attacks partially succeed in up to 86% of cases, but agents often fail to fully complete the attacker's goal, which the authors call 'security by incompetence'.
US [webresearch]: Evidence that browsing agents do get hijacked. A more capable open brain (for example a better search model) makes injections more likely to succeed end to end, so tool isolation has to come before capability upgrades.
CORRECTION [webresearch]: The abstract confirms attacks partially succeed in up to 86% of cases, 'security by incompetence', and simple low-effort human-written injections that deceive top models, including reasoning models.
